text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Parliament gave conceptual approval to the next year's budget draft at an extraordinary session on Monday with 65 votes in favour, 16 against and one abstention. It's likely the budget's final reading will take place late November.

- Russia is soon to replace its ambassador to Latvia. Alexander Rannikh will be succeeded by Serguey Udaltsov, deputy director of the Second European Department of the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
- Several hundreds of teachers held a picket near parliament on Monday to protest about low wages.
- The board of political party Latvia's Way has called on the governing factions to announce a moratorium on further reshuffling of the parliament's presidium.

- The Higher Commissioner for Human Rights of the OSCE, Max van der Stoel, arrived on a two-day working visit in Latvia. He will meet Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs, President Guntis Ulmanis and Education Minister Maris Grinblats.
- The Ministry of Finance has lodged two suits for debts against the Riga heating comapany, Rigas Siltums.
